text:
maria: Quick sync — noticed some blind spots in the batcher telemetry that are blocking continuous-batching heuristic tuning. Specifically: per-pod KV cache hit rate correlated with average batch size, token/sec ingress vs egress per queue (to surface token budget throttling), and a clearer batch-utilization metric (not just batch_size distribution).

chris: +1. Current dashboard only shows avg batch size and queue depth. We need p50/p95 batch utilization, p95 queue depth, and a token-budget burn-rate (tokens consumed / token budget) per model. Alerts for sustained low utilization too. :eyes: 

sameer: For queries, rough PromQL for KV hit rate by pod: 
```
sum by(pod) (rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum by(pod) (rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))
```
And batch utilization (tokens emitted / theoretical capacity):
```
avg by(pod) (sum(rate(batcher_tokens_processed_total[1m])) / (sum(rate(batcher_capacity_tokens_total[1m])) + 1e-9))
```
Token budget burn-rate (per-request rolling 1m):
```
sum by(request_id) (rate(request_tokens_consumed_total[1m])) / max(1, request_token_budget)
```
These are rough; we should tag by `model` and `seq_len_bucket` so we can route heuristics per-workload.

lucy: UX ask: please surface a histogram panel for batch size + a separate heatmap for seq_len_bucket vs batch_utilization. Also add a table that lists pods with KV hit%, avg batch size, and recent OOM/restart counts — assists triage.

maria: For alerts: 1) KV hit rate < 10% for 10m on >= 50% of pods -> ticket + paging candidate (could mean cache warmup/regression). 2) avg batch_utilization < 30% for 15m -> we should recommend increasing token_budget or open autoscale. 3) sustained token burn-rate > budget on >= 5% requests -> rollout rollback guard. Thoughts?

chris: Sounds good. For the KV alert, add a suppression window after deploy (10m) to avoid noisy false positives. For utilization alert, make it informational first (Pager: no) and escalate if it persists across 2 windows.

infra-bot: grafana: new panel PR created by @chris -> https://git.internal/grafana/dash/1123 (WIP) :rocket:

maria: Nice. Two operational requirements: 1) store 1s resolution for token/sec metrics for 1 hour, 10s resolution for 24h, and roll up to 1m for 30d. 2) label ingestion pipeline with `deployment_id` and `model_version` so we can correlate regressions to rollouts.

sameer: Implementation note: the batcher emits `batcher_capacity_tokens_total` in a non-monotonic way currently (we discovered in profiling). I'll instrument kernel-selection path to emit stable capacity counters and add a delta-guard in the Prometheus exporter. That should make the utilization query reliable.

lucy: Dash layout proposal: Top row: overall cluster KPIs (tokens/sec, avg batch_utilization, p95 queue_depth). Middle: per-model heatmaps + KV hit rate by pod. Bottom: incidents & recent deploys panel.

maria: I'll open a lightweight GH issue with the panel list + the promql snippets, assign to @chris for the PR and @dash-team for review. sameer: can you add the exporter fix and link the commit in the issue?

chris: Will do. Aiming for PR by end of day tomorrow.

dash-team: Happy to review layout and alert wording. Can you add sample screenshots / wireframe to the issue?

maria: Perfect. If no blockers, let's roll this into the next infra sprint. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

chris: +1

infra-bot: deploy-batcher-exporter: patch queued for staging (build #4217)

maria: marking follow-ups: GH-#2742 (dashboard panels), GH-#2743 (exporter stability), alert-runbook draft in the issue.

lucy: Adding runbook notes for triage on KV regressions (cache warmup, eviction storms, model skew).

maria: closing — if anyone thinks we missed other telemetry for continuous batching tuning, reply here or add to GH-#2742.
